headline: Running still hasn't returned — the gap since the trail block is now a real off-stretch. One recent lift, no rhythm yet. The base underneath remains deep and intact.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is unchanged in shape but longer in duration: no running has re-entered, and the single strength session logged mid-week hasn't yet become a cadence. What holds the load up right now is background movement — daily step volume stays high even on nominal rest days, which is the only thing keeping this from being a true full stop. The recent four-week running block was enormous relative to the prior month, so an extended down-period reads as legitimate absorption from that trail load rather than drift. But the length now matters: the top-end and structured stimulus have both been quiet long enough that this is a deliberate off-block, not a reset. Recovery signals are mixed and noisy, and don't independently justify extending the pause further.
sections.trends: Year-to-date distance is running dramatically ahead of the same point last year, and the 12-week base is substantial — the long arc is clearly building, not eroding. The recent shape is a big cyclical spike (the trail block) followed by a trough, which is a normal breathing pattern for a year-round hybrid approach that doesn't strictly periodise. That shape makes sense. What would start to conflict with the standing goals is if the trough flattens into a plateau with no re-entry — cyclical is healthy, open-ended is not.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the VO2max picture are unchanged and stem from a benchmark now well over a month old, taken before the trail block. Nothing in the recent running touches that intensity band, so there's no new evidence either way — the number is stale rather than declining. Demonstrated threshold fitness remains intact on paper; the question is simply that it hasn't been tested recently. Don't read the quiet top end as a loss until a faster effort actually reappears and gives a fresh reading.
sections.zones: The recent runs were almost entirely low-aerobic, ceiling-capped efforts — appropriate for the durability intent of a trail block, and the per-session shapes confirm that character rather than hiding harder work under a soft average. That distribution was correct for what that block was doing. But the block is over, and there's been essentially no upper-zone stimulus since. For a hybrid athlete the grey zone isn't the risk here — the absence of any Z4/Z5 exposure for an extended stretch is. The intensity distribution was right for absorption; it's now overdue for a spike at the top.
sections.hr_comparison: The most recent lift logged without HR, so there's little new to read on strength intensity. Where strength HR does exist, it sits in the expected moderate band for functional work, and the Polar-derived strength figures track sensibly against the running data without any obvious mismatch. Nothing anomalous in source agreement worth flagging.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the real story more clearly than any single metric: a dense, high-volume running cluster followed by a clean break, with only one strength touch since. The running frequency has gone from consistent to absent, and strength hasn't stepped in to fill the structural gap with repetition. Steps remain the one uninterrupted thread. This is a genuine pause in structured training, not a light week — the consistency pattern has broken, and the coming days decide whether it re-knits.
sections.personal_bests: None are in reach right now — the short-distance PBs need sharp, fast running that hasn't featured at all recently, and the current state is post-block quiet rather than sharpening. The ultra-distance bests remain the most aligned with this athlete's demonstrated durability, but they aren't approached from a trough either. PBs are a question for once structured work resumes, not for this week.

watch_items: Watch whether running finally re-enters this week, or whether the off-stretch tips from deliberate into unplanned.
Watch whether the single recent lift becomes a repeated strength cadence rather than another isolated touch.
Watch for the first faster or upper-zone effort — the top end has now been dormant unusually long and needs a fresh reading.
Watch that the first easy run returns at a normal easy HR, confirming the trail block absorbed cleanly.
